critical_code_review_comments: Bug fixed during this iteration: /api/companies/me/landing-leads used `async for ... in db.find(...).to_list(500):` — to_list() returns a Future, not an async iterable, so admin GET threw 500. Rewrote to `leads = await db.find(...).to_list(500); return leads`. This pattern should be audited elsewhere; grep for any other `async for .* to_list` occurrences.

/api/public/landing-lead has no rate-limit and no CAPTCHA — anyone can spam any company_id endlessly. Consider IP-throttling + per-company daily caps; problem statement notes this is acceptable for now.

Lead update endpoint /api/companies/me/landing-leads/{lead_id}/status exists (good) but there is no DELETE endpoint; test leads accumulate. Add admin delete or hard-delete after status=lost+older-than-X.
AdminDashboard.jsx still 2454+ lines (flagged in iter 31, no progress).

TenantPublicLanding receives raw `host` query param trust on the same-origin call from frontend — server-side _normalize_host strips port/www correctly; SYSTEM_HOSTS_SUFFIXES list blocks emergent/surirent/localhost. Solid.

rca_of_the_issue: ONE backend bug found and fixed: GET /api/companies/me/landing-leads used `async for lead in db.landing_leads.find(...).sort(...).to_list(500):` — `.to_list()` returns an awaitable Future, NOT an async iterable, so the request raised TypeError: 'async for' requires an object with __aiter__ method. Fix: `leads = await db.landing_leads.find(...).sort(...).to_list(500); return leads`. After fix, admin lead-list endpoint returns 200 with the test lead included. All other endpoints worked first try.
